title: Semi-Final Pitching: Proving success by transitioning Product development into real-world usage
image1Description: Presenting product progress (Product Demo) to the Project Manager judging panel in the Semi-Final round

section1.heading: Origin and Intent
section1.content: In the Semi-Final round of the Tuek Som Garage project, the key challenge was no longer just about the idea, but proving that the product we had been developing 'works in reality' and 'solves the right problems.' My intent for this round was to demonstrate the progress of the TaladHub system, showing its transformation from a blueprint into functional software. This was to instill confidence in the committee that the project had sufficient potential to evolve into a real corporate business.

section2.heading: Role and Action
section2.content: I served as the lead for the Product Progress Report, presenting to a committee of professional Team Leads and Project Managers from various departments. I conducted a live Demo of the system's core completed components, specifically highlighting functions that addressed the real-world user pain points we had researched. I also showcased the system Architecture's readiness to support future expansion, allowing the judges to see the feasibility of deploying the system on a larger scale.

section3.heading: Challenges
section3.content: The challenge in this round was addressing technical and project management inquiries from experts (PMs), who focused on stability, data security, and development cost-efficiency. I had to prepare data to confirm that every feature included created actual business value, rather than just being a 'nice-to-have' function. Handling constructive criticism directly from project professionals helped me gain a more comprehensive perspective on development.

section4.heading: Results and Learning
section4.content: Due to a clear presentation and a tangible product, we successfully advanced to the Final Pitching round—the final stage where we present to high-level Executives. This Semi-Final experience developed my skills in 'Product Validation' and managing expectations for management-level stakeholders. I learned that the success of software lies in its ability to solve people's problems in the simplest and most powerful way possible.
